nD.text:
Profile

- Five sections on the left; the open section’s fields on the right. Save and continue saves the whole profile.
- Location (owner decision): type the address into the map search, pick a match, then drag the pin onto the entrance. The pin also moves with the arrow keys. Latitude and longitude are saved on the profile; the address fields stay editable.
- New states: searching (matches listed), no match (fill the address and drag the pin by hand), pin placed, pin moved by the owner.
- Out-of-area errors sit on Postal code. Cuisines still need a lookup the restaurant can read (Needs API).
- Welcome back is a local draft on this device; Finish later keeps it there.
- Session ended during save: sign in again in the page, not in a modal; the save is retried with the same values.

nE.text:
Documents

- Four required documents in the list; the selected one opens beside it. Liability insurance is hidden until V2 (owner decision).
- Upload through the FileDrop, then add the details. Valid until is required for the halal certificate, food safety and owner ID.
- A person checks every document within 3 business days (owner decision); the copy quotes it.
- Send for review is never disabled; it is primary only at 4 of 4.
- In review is neutral. Warnings are for real faults only; never red on the halal certificate.
- Download makes a new link on each click (2 minutes); the file downloads.

nF.text:
Review and fix

- List of the four documents, the selected one beside it. The restaurant never sees the seven halal check results.
- Reviews take up to 3 business days (owner decision).
- An expired certificate during review is slate in the banner, the row and the checklist. No seal on a document row.
- One primary per page. When a re-upload can’t fix it (certifier, forgery, duplicate), Call partner support is the primary.
- Rejection labels come from Ref-Rejections; reviewer notes are verbatim.

nG.text:
Payout

- Status on the left, the next step on the right.
- During setup, payouts must be on before the menu step.
- Paused payouts on a live restaurant (owner decision): the restaurant keeps taking orders; earnings build up and Stripe pays them out once it has what it needs. Payout-PastDue shows a new order arriving in the header strip meanwhile.
- Stripe requirement names stay verbatim but secondary.

tH.text: First menu (added by the restaurant, reviewed by HalalGoes) and opening hours

nH.text:
Menu and hours at launch

- Restaurants add and edit their own menu at launch, with the HalalGoes menu review queue (owner decision). Prices, preparation times and availability go live at once; names, descriptions, ingredients, allergens and photos are checked first.
- The menu is published when a reviewer approves the first item.
- The restaurant sets its own opening hours: each day Closed or up to 3 ranges, past midnight allowed. Times are 12-hour (owner decision).
- Menu-None: nothing added yet. Menu-V0: the first item is live and two are with a reviewer.

tK.text: Withdrawn, account states and setup blockers

nK.text:
Ends, account states and setup blockers

- Withdraw asks for confirmation in the page, not in a modal (Needs API: withdraw).
- Suspended during setup shows the reason in plain language, with a fallback only when it’s empty. Documents stay reachable.
- A certificate that lapses during setup is a setup blocker, not delisting: the account stays pending, the seal shows Expired in slate, and nothing mentions a listing. Delisting only happens to a live restaurant (live console row).
- The renewal opens in the right pane, as an in-page panel.
- Deactivated is the restaurant’s own reversible exit (Reactivate: Needs API).
- Banned and closed restaurants never see setup: their sessions end and sign-in explains why (SignIn-Banned, SignIn-RestaurantClosed).

tK2.text: Live console for account states: new orders in a header strip, no Kanban

nK2.text:
Live console for account states

- No Kanban. New orders live in a persistent strip in the header (owner decision: under the app bar): each shows its 180-second countdown; arrow keys move, A accepts and R rejects the focused order only; reject asks for a reason in an in-page panel.
- Orders list on the left, the selected order on the right. Orders in progress render from their own status.
- Side navigation is collapsible. Staff is gone (owner only).
- The renewed-certificate form opens as an in-page panel beside the list.

tR.text: Reflow at 320 CSS px (1280 at 400% zoom): onboarding after the email link

nR.text:
Reflow

- Restaurant web runs on desktop and on landscape tablets from 1024 × 768 (owner decision); portrait tablet and phone layouts are gone.
- These boards are the 400% zoom check: the setup pages reflow to one column at 320 CSS px with no sideways scrolling.
- They use the stacked parts (ProfileMain, DocsMain, ReviewMain, PayoutMain, MenuMain, HoursBlock); desktop uses the pane parts.
- A photo is one page: multi-page certificates need a PDF until the API takes several files per document.

tI.text: Shared parts (edit once, every screen updates)

nI.text:
Parts

- Desktop setup: OnbTop, OnbSide (collapsible rail), and one pane part per step: ProfilePanes, DocsPanes, ReviewPanes, PayoutPanes, MenuPanes, AccountState (with RenewCert).
- 400% zoom reflow and tablet: the stacked parts in the second half of this row.
- Each part has a mode switch in Tweaks: edit once, every screen updates.

readme.text:
How to read this canvas

- Restaurant web, light theme only (owner decision). Desktop screens are 1440 × 900 and never scroll: long lists scroll inside their own pane, detail opens in panes beside the list, and nothing that is work opens in a modal or sheet.
- Owner only at launch: one login per restaurant, no staff or manager accounts, no restaurant switcher.
- Screens compose the HalalGoes design system (Button, IconButton, Input, Select, Checkbox, Switch, Badge, Card, Menu, AppBar, Countdown, Price, HalalBadge, HalalCertificationPanel). Dashed outlines tagged “Proposed component: …” are composites built from library parts (shadcn/ui on web) and system parts, for the owner to approve into the design system. FileDrop, KeyValueList and SideNav are already approved; Split panes, Collapsible sidebar, Detail panel and the New-orders strip come from the desktop layout rules.
- Dashed blue “Needs API: …” chips mark data the contract lacks (all on Ref-NeedsAPI). Grey mono tags are annotations, not UI.
- Onboarding is server-driven: screens render current_step, progress and review round as returned; the client never works out the next step.
- Sample data: Zaytoun Grill, owner Samir Haddad. Dates are absolute. [support phone] and [support hours] come from the public config.
- Colour uses role tokens from the design system’s tokens.css (recompiled 28 September 2026); no local token overrides.
